scenes.title: The price of clarity
scenes.narration: What if the biggest pricing mistake isn't a wrong number, but comparing two things that were never equivalent in the first place?

cues.text: What if the biggest pricing mistake isn't a wrong number,
but comparing two things that were never
equivalent in the first place?
¿Y si el mayor error de precios no fuera una cifra equivocada,
sino comparar dos cosas que nunca fueron equivalentes?

scenes.title: Define the product first
scenes.narration: A publishing catalogue looks simple: a title, a series and a price. But behind every title sit formats, levels, editions, packs and access rights.

cues.text: A publishing catalogue looks simple: a title,
a series and a price.
But behind every title sit formats, levels, editions,
packs and access rights.
Un catálogo editorial parece sencillo: un título,
una serie y un precio.
Pero detrás de cada título hay formatos, niveles, ediciones,
packs y derechos de acceso.

scenes.title: A fictional catalogue
scenes.narration: For this case study I generated a fictional catalogue: three hundred and sixty-two products, twelve series, and data problems planted on purpose. No real publisher, no real prices.

cues.text: For this case study I generated a fictional catalogue:
three hundred and sixty-two products, twelve series,
and data problems planted on purpose.
No real publisher, no real prices.
Para este caso generé un catálogo inventado:
trescientos sesenta y dos productos,
doce series y problemas de datos sembrados a propósito.
Ni editorial real ni precios reales.

scenes.title: Five columns in, nineteen out
scenes.narration: First, I recovered structure from the titles, without guessing. If a title doesn't mention access duration, that's unknown, not unlimited.

cues.text: First, I recovered structure from the titles, without guessing.
If a title doesn't mention access duration,
that's unknown, not unlimited.
Primero recuperé la estructura de los títulos, sin adivinar.
Si un título no menciona la duración del
acceso, es desconocida, no ilimitada.

scenes.title: Keep the source
scenes.narration: The raw file stays untouched. Every correction lives in a separate, reversible reporting view, so any number traces back to its source record.

cues.text: The raw file stays untouched.
Every correction lives in a separate, reversible reporting view,
so any number traces back to its source record.
El fichero original no se toca.
Cada corrección vive en una vista
de reporting aparte y reversible,
así que cualquier cifra se puede rastrear hasta su registro.

scenes.title: Two misfiled records
scenes.narration: Two records carry a series name that contradicts their own title. They're flagged and re-filed in the reporting view, never silently overwritten.

cues.text: Two records carry a series name that
contradicts their own title.
They're flagged and re-filed in the reporting view,
never silently overwritten.
Dos registros llevan un nombre de serie
que contradice su propio título.
Se señalan y se reubican en la vista de reporting,
nunca se sobrescriben en silencio.

scenes.title: Gleebook is not an eBook
scenes.narration: A printed resource called Gleebook contains the letters e-book. A naive substring rule grants it digital access. A word-boundary rule doesn't.

cues.text: A printed resource called Gleebook contains the letters e-book.
A naive substring rule grants it digital access.
A word-boundary rule doesn't.
Un recurso impreso llamado Gleebook contiene las letras «ebook».
Una regla ingenua por subcadena le concede acceso digital;
una regla con límites de palabra, no.

scenes.title: Like for like
scenes.narration: Only then did I compare prices: same series, type, pack, edition and access. Only the level is allowed to change. That gives sixty comparable groups.

cues.text: Only then did I compare prices: same series,
type, pack, edition and access.
Only the level is allowed to change.
That gives sixty comparable groups.
Solo entonces comparé precios: misma
serie, tipo, pack, edición y acceso.
Solo puede cambiar el nivel.
Así salen sesenta grupos comparables.

scenes.title: 54 of 60, then 56
scenes.narration: Fifty-four of the sixty hold one price at every level. Four exceptions are cheaper Starter levels. The other two aren't pricing at all: they're filing errors.

cues.text: Fifty-four of the sixty hold one price at every level.
Four exceptions are cheaper Starter levels.
The other two aren't pricing at all: they're filing errors.
Cincuenta y cuatro de los sesenta mantienen
un mismo precio en todos los niveles.
Cuatro excepciones son niveles Starter más baratos.
Las otras dos no son precios: son errores de archivo.

scenes.title: Two parts cost more
scenes.narration: Matched comparisons show more. Buying a book in two parts costs about fourteen percent more than the complete volume, at every level.

cues.text: Matched comparisons show more.
Buying a book in two parts costs about fourteen percent
more than the complete volume, at every level.
Las comparaciones emparejadas muestran más:
comprar un libro en dos partes cuesta en torno a un
catorce por ciento más que el volumen completo,
en todos los niveles.

scenes.title: What the data can't say
scenes.narration: But list prices alone can't show demand, costs or margins. Without sales and discount data, a recommended price would be speculation.

cues.text: But list prices alone can't show demand, costs or margins.
Without sales and discount data,
a recommended price would be speculation.

es.title: Lo que los datos no pueden decir

cues.text: Pero los precios de catálogo no muestran
demanda, costes ni márgenes.
Sin datos de ventas y descuentos,
recomendar un precio sería especular.

scenes.title: A chain of decisions
scenes.narration: So the result isn't a dashboard. It's a method: keep the source, recover the structure, compare like with like, and say what you don't know.

cues.text: So the result isn't a dashboard.
It's a method: keep the source, recover the structure,
compare like with like, and say what you don't know.
Así que el resultado no es un dashboard.
Es un método: conservar el origen, recuperar la estructura,
comparar lo comparable y decir lo que no sabes.

scenes.title: 362 fictional products
scenes.narration: I built a pricing case study on three hundred and sixty-two fictional textbooks. The hard part wasn't the average.

cues.text: I built a pricing case study on three hundred
and sixty-two fictional textbooks.
The hard part wasn't the average.
Construí un caso de precios con trescientos
sesenta y dos libros de texto ficticios.
Lo difícil no era la media.

scenes.title: Gleebook ≠ eBook
scenes.narration: It was the traps: misfiled series, ambiguous bundles, and a Gleebook that a naive parser reads as an e-book.

cues.text: It was the traps: misfiled series, ambiguous bundles,
and a Gleebook that a naive parser reads as an e-book.
Eran las trampas: series mal archivadas,
packs ambiguos y un «Gleebook» que un
parser ingenuo toma por un e-book.

scenes.narration: Matched like for like, fifty-four of sixty groups hold one price. Two of the six exceptions were filing errors.

cues.text: Matched like for like,

Two of the six exceptions were filing errors.
Comparando lo comparable,
cincuenta y cuatro de sesenta grupos mantienen un precio.
Dos de las seis excepciones eran errores de archivo.
